devices.label: IBM Heron r1 (Torino)
devices.description: IBM's 133-qubit Heron processor: a heavy-hex lattice, every qubit coupled to two or three neighbours.

devices.label: IBM Flamingo, 1 QPU
devices.description: A Flamingo QPU as modelled here: the 127-qubit Eagle heavy-hex lattice extended to 133 qubits.

devices.label: IBM Flamingo, 3 QPUs
devices.description: Three Flamingo QPUs in a chain, each linked to the next by four l-couplers (remote, 3% error, 300 ns).

devices.label: IBM Loon/Nighthawk, 1 QPU
devices.description: An 11 by 11 square lattice with long-range c-couplers (IBM's large-scale fault-tolerance roadmap). As modelled, the c-couplers start from the first row of the lattice only.

devices.label: IBM Loon/Nighthawk, 2 QPUs
devices.description: Two Loon QPUs linked by four l-couplers.

devices.label: IBM bicycle architecture module
devices.description: The 288 qubits of the gross code in its toric layout: four couplers to neighbours on a torus and two long-range c-couplers per qubit, all as good as local couplers.
devices.sweep_label: IBM bicycle module: gross-code toric layout with long-range c-couplers (288 qubits)

devices.label: IBM bicycle module, noisy c-couplers
devices.description: The bicycle architecture module with its c-couplers as noisy and slow as remote couplers.
devices.sweep_label: IBM bicycle module with c-couplers as noisy as remote couplers (288 qubits)

devices.label: IBM bicycle modules, 2 chained
devices.description: Two bicycle architecture modules linked by four remote couplers, for codes larger than one module.

devices.label: Google Willow (extended)
devices.description: Willow's square lattice in the shape of a diamond, extended to 315 qubits.

devices.label: Quantinuum Apollo
devices.description: Trapped ions: neighbours on the grid interact in place, any other pair after moving an ion (shuttling).

devices.label: Infleqtion (neutral atoms)
devices.description: Neutral atoms on a grid: neighbours interact in place, any other pair after moving an atom.

devices.label: Infleqtion, no shuttling
devices.description: Infleqtion's array restricted to nearest-neighbour gates.

devices.label: Harvard/MIT neutral-atom array
devices.description: The reconfigurable 448-atom array of Bluvstein et al. (Nature 2025): any pair interacts after a move, which costs a gate error and atom loss.

devices.label: Diamond grid
devices.description: A square lattice in the shape of a diamond, like Willow's, into which the rotated surface code fits.

devices.label: All-to-all
devices.description: Every pair of qubits is coupled.
